abstract: A new variety of hybrid lily plant bearing large upright to semi-upright flowers particularly characterized by their unspotted, pure white coloration with a soft pink reverse side. The flowers of this new plant are of excellent form and with their large size and substance, orientation and color, provide a combination that is completely new in the Oriental hybrid divisions of lilies suited to forcing and mass commercial cultivation. The plant is highly resistant to disease, shows tolerance of virus, and is an excellent garden plant. The bulbs of this plant may be precooled and forced for cut flower production, the resulting clone being vigorous, a good grower, and an excellent propagator.

Four-stroke-cycle engines; driving-gear; casings.-In a revolving-cylinder engine the cylinders are arranged in pairs tangential to a circle around the shaft b; the pistons carry pairs of rollers f, h which engage on the two sides of a stationary cam rail i. The combustible mixture enters the combustion chamber n and the exhaust leaves through one valve-controlled port; a short passage z connects this port in sequence to a supply passage s<1> and exhaust pipe t<1> formed in the gearing u for the shaft, one set of passage and pipe serving two cylinders. Instead of the two rollers f, h engaging the same cam rail, a separate roller d<1> may be provided for each piston to engage a separate cam for ensuring the movement of the piston on its suction stroke. The cam is shaped to give a longer exhaust than compression stroke. The four cylinders forming the engine are enclosed in a casing k supporting the cams. The valves are held open during the whole of the suction and exhaust strokes.

143,386. Morton, C. H. May 15, 1919. Folding seats.-A seat is adapted to be alternatively employed in an upright position with a horizontal seat, or in a lounge position with a flexible seat, by different settings of the chair supports. Fig. 1 shows the seat in the first position, the member A acting as a back-rest, while in Fig. 2 the whole chair is shown tilted over on its supports, the flexible material L then acting as the seat member. The seat may be folded after removing the pins F from the slots E.

241,478. Hinz, H. May 11, 1925. No Patent granted (Sealing fee not paid). Type cases.-A sorts box f, Fig. 3, for special types, is provided with a hook e by which it is attached to the side wall m of the usual type case n, and a spring i on the front wall h of the box serves to retain the hook in engagement. A number of such boxes f are stored in a storage case a, Fig. 1, with their hooks e engaging longitudinal ledges or partitions b, the distance between the ledges being greater than the length of the boxes in order to facilitate the withdrawal of the latter. The bottoms of the boxes rest upon longitudinal strips d which are also of less width than the distance between the ledges b, thereby providing at one side a channel down which any types that may be dropped can slide down to the rounded front edge of the storage case, which is inclined in the usual manner.

214,470. Jackson, R. R. May 7, 1923. Brakes, arrangement and disposition of. - An auxiliary contracting brake for operation in conjunction with, and acting upon, the exterior of the same drum as the usual internal expanding brake of a motor vehicle, particularly of the Ford type, is arranged to be directly connected to the existing brake rod provided for connection to the cam lever of the internal brake which is instead connected to or engaged by the lever of the external brake. The auxiliary brake band 18 has its ends 20, 21 connected to a two-armed lever 9 on a spindle 8 passing through bosses 7, Fig. 3, on a bracket 1 which has a hole and a slotted end 5 by which it is fixed to the disc on the axle casing by the bolts 4 which secure the radius rod 2. Studs 6 are also provided on the bracket to contact with the disc. The band is supported by two spring-urged pins 19 passing through a member 16 which is secured by the bolt 17 upon which the internal brake shoes are pivoted and is held further by the engagement of one of the ribs 16 on the disc in a, groove in the member. The spindle 8 carries an operating arm 10 to which the existing rod 15 is connected at 11 and this arm is adapted to engage the cam lever 12 of the internal brake so that this brake is applied after the band brake has come into operation. In a modified arrangement, the bracket 1 is inverted so that the spindle 8 and arm 9 are carried above the radius rod 2 and the end of the arm 10 and the rod 15 are below the rod 2. In this case the arm 10 is connected by a link to the cam lever 12 and the two brakes are brought into operation simultaneously.

520.017. Ironing-presses. GEORGE, H., and BROWN & GREEN, Ltd. April 24, 1939, No. 12236. [Class 138 (ii)] The buck 25 of a pressing-machine, particularly for ironing collars, cuffs and shirt yokes, is carried by a frame 24 pivoted at 26 to a ram 8. A link 27 is pivoted between a stationary pin 29 and a pin 28 on the frame 24. On admitting fluid pressure to the cylinder 6 from a valve 10, constructed as described in Specification 495,660, [Group XXIX], and operated by spaced manuals 14, the frame is swung and raised so that the buck coacts with the stationary head 3. The cylinder is exhausted by depression of a. treadle 13 which actuates the valve 10 in the reverse direction. Shock absorbers 31, 35 are provided to cushion the opening and closing movements of the press.
